headline: Apple: mixing languages beats fine-tuning
dek: Apple tested four model sizes and about 1,000 training runs, with Arabic as the low-resource language, Apple Machine Learning says.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: A rich language helps a poor one
body: Apple published a study on training models for languages with little data, such as Arabic (Apple Machine Learning).
According to the research, mixing in an abundant language like English beats hyperparameter tuning.

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: The two techniques compared
s3.body: According to Apple, the study pitted two pre-training strategies:

points.t: Raising weight decay, a form of regularization (Apple).
Adding auxiliary-language data to the scarce target data (Apple).
From 150 million to 1.43 billion parameters, trained from scratch (Apple Machine Learning).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: The gap grows with model size
body: According to Apple, mixing beat tuning on validation loss and on downstream task accuracy.
The company says the effect equals having two to three times more target-language data on validation loss.

items.t: The research suggests mixing an abundant language into training (Apple).
The test used Arabic and English; other languages were not evaluated.
The study did not test Portuguese, according to Apple's material.

caption.hook: Apple says mixing languages in training beats fine-tuning for languages with little data.
body: According to Apple Machine Learning, the study compared two pre-training strategies using Arabic as the low-resource language and English as the auxiliary. It covered four model sizes, from 150 million to 1.43 billion parameters, across about 1,000 training runs.

The company says language mixing beat hyperparameter tuning on validation loss and on downstream task accuracy, and that the gap grows with model size. The study tested only Arabic and English, so the same cannot be said for other languages.
